consensus_expectations: FY2026 consensus (22 analysts, Capital IQ, pulled 2026-08-13, SHSE/China-GAAP/CNY series): revenue CNY 309,111mn (+2.24% YoY, a sharp deceleration from FY2025's +5.71%), EBITDA CNY 30,506mn, EPS CNY 2.13 (+1.4% YoY). No formal management guidance exists for consolidated revenue/EBITDA/EPS (last CapIQ Guidance-tab entry is FH1 2012); the only quantified forward disclosures are a >=58% FY2026 dividend-payout floor and 'high single-digit' CCR segment revenue growth. Consensus has been cut sharply over the trailing 6-12 months: FY2026 EPS down ~14.1% (6mo) / ~13.4% (12mo); FY2026 revenue down ~4.8% (12mo). Revision breadth is net negative into the H1 2026 print (2026-08-27/28): EPS 1 up / 11 down, gross margin 3 up / 20 down. The last two reported quarters (FQ4 2025, FQ1 2026) both missed the already-cut consensus, and the FY2025 annual print missed by -7.1% on EPS. Bar assessment: 'Bar is high -- miss risk elevated' [earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md §7]. No analyst mean target price is reported anywhere in this run's outputs (not surfaced by guidance-consensus or price-and-capital-structure).
market_implied_expectations: Reverse-DCF (valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md), holding the DCF module's own WACC (4.10%, CAPM-derived) and 7.0x terminal EV/EBITDA exit multiple fixed: the CNY 21.75 price requires either a sustained -6.48%/yr FCF/EBITDA contraction through FY2030 (cumulative -28.4%) or a steady-state EBIT margin of 4.40% -- a new low, below Haier's own FY2021 trough (5.91%) and below the DCF module's own dedicated structural-decline bear case (5.00%). Neither has precedent in Haier's disclosed 5-year history (revenue has never posted a full-year decline; FCF fell in only 1 of 5 years and fully rebounded the next). This literal reading argues the market is pricing historically-unprecedented pessimism -- a potential undervaluation signal. But the module itself flags this as entangled with an unusually low WACC: a flat, no-growth FCF trajectory reconciles to the current price at a ~12.3% discount rate -- a far more ordinary rate for a China-listed industrial than the CAPM-derived 4.10% the primary solve is forced to use. The module explicitly calls the finding two-sided and inconclusive, 'not a standalone conviction driver,' and the final thesis carries that caveat forward verbatim.
engine_view: Base-case fair value CNY 23.67/share (+8.8% vs price), from a 5-method triangulation (peer-relative valuation weighted 68%, intrinsic DCF, own-history multiples, sum-of-the-parts, reverse-DCF as a cross-check, not a lever) [valuation/07_scenario-and-fair-value.md]. Scenario levels: bull CNY 31.78 (+46.1%, 20% prob) / base CNY 23.67 (+8.8%, 40% prob) / bear-cyclical CNY 16.79 (-22.8%, 25% prob) / bear-structural CNY 15.90 (-26.9%, 15% prob). Margin of safety to base case: 8.1%; downside to headline bear: 26.9%. Probability-weighted expected return +3.02% (target CNY 22.41); risk/reward 0.11 -- poor. Individual methods diverge widely: peer-relative (the dominant, market-anchored method, real dated comps) finds only a +1.5% quality-adjusted residual (CNY 22.08 vs CNY 21.75) once Haier's below-peer margins (EBIT 6.9% vs Midea 9.8%, Gree 17.4%) and confirmed-eroding moat are adjusted for -- 'mostly, not fully' explained by fundamentals; intrinsic DCF finds CNY 29.84 (+37.2%, capped to Moderate confidence because the WACC is flagged as too low); SOTP finds CNY 23.86 (+9.7%, but comp-fragile -- 43% of the spread rides on one segment's peer choice). Overall module verdict: 'Fairly valued,' not cheap. Final headline decision: Watchlist -- explicitly not a Buy, on the grounds that the +3.0% expected return does not compensate for 26.9% downside risk into a print whose own setup favors a miss.
what_everyone_knows: Haier trades at a 25-38% discount to Midea/Gree/Whirlpool on every reported multiple; its margins (EBIT 6.9%) trail both named Chinese peers (Midea 9.8%, Gree 17.4%); China's appliance trade-in subsidy is fading and raw-material costs are rising; the last two reported quarters both missed consensus; consensus has already been cut ~14% over six months.
what_is_priced_in: Most of the known bad news. The dominant, market-anchored valuation method (peer-relative, 68% weight) finds that once Haier's below-peer margin and confirmed-eroding moat are quality-adjusted for, the residual gap to peers shrinks to a modest +1.5% (CNY 22.08 fair value vs CNY 21.75 price) -- essentially fair value, not a bargain. The reverse-DCF's literal reading (a -6.48%/yr FCF contraction) would argue the market is pricing MORE pessimism than the evidence supports, but the module itself discounts this as likely a mechanical artefact of an unusually low CAPM WACC rather than genuine mispricing.
what_market_may_be_missing: Two modest points, per the engine's own framing: (1) the common 'China SOE-adjacent governance discount' story does not apply here -- management-governance explicitly tested for a structurally misaligned controlling owner (CLAUDE.md §24 Filter 6) and did not find one (no pledging, no dual-class stock, cumulative voting); the discount is an earnings-trajectory discount, not an ownership discount. evidence_engine_is_different: Weak. The run's own pre_mortem.json (variant_perception_attack) adversarially tested both components and found: (1) the ownership-discount correction is a negative claim (rules out a story) that does not by itself justify paying more -- it does not demonstrate the market is missing anything, since the valuation module's own quality-adjusted residual is only +1.5%, within the noise band of a peer-multiple adjustment; (2) the forensic mosaic rests entirely on data already sitting in Haier's own public RPT footnotes, subsidy-classification language and accrual/receivables/inventory trends -- the kind of screen 'any diligent buy-side or forensic-accounting desk runs routinely' -- and the dossier presents no evidence this specific combination is absent from sell-side coverage or consensus positioning. The engine's own final_thesis text concurs, self-labelling the edge 'real but modest ... not a strong, proprietary insight the market has missed' and capping conviction to 60 regardless of the rest of the dossier via its own edge gate (edge_score 25/100 < 50 threshold).
base_rate_check: Per the pre-mortem's base_rate_check (three tests matched to the claim's own metric/level/period, CLAUDE.md §9): (1) sell-side revision momentum after two consecutive misses with net-negative breadth (1 up/11 down EPS) is typically a continuation signal over a one-quarter horizon, not mean-reverting -- the dossier's own 35% beat-probability forecast is consistent with, not more pessimistic than, this base rate; (2) margin stabilization for a hard-goods manufacturer with 84% of COGS in un-passed-through commodities, after a cost-reduction program FY2025's own MD&A calls 'overwhelmed,' has no base-rate support for sudden near-term stabilization; (3) the bull case's two-condition conjunction (commodity-cost reversion to 0pp AND China demand recovery to +5% YoY) at 20% probability is a genuine, correctly-flagged conjunction, and 20% reads as defensible, not generous, given neither leg is yet evidenced. None of the three tests suggest the engine is understating downside risk or making an exceptional forecast without exceptional evidence -- the near-term forecast-ledger probabilities already lean appropriately cautious.
